chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hakam al-A'ma and Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who gave permission to his slave regarding a free woman, so he married her. Then the slave fled from his masters, and the slave’s wife came seeking her maintenance from the master of the slave. So he said: She has no maintenance due from the master of the slave, and her marital bond with him has been severed, because the slave’s flight is the divorce of his wife, and he is in the position of one who has apostatized from Islam. I said: Then if he returns to his master, does his wife return to him? He said: If her waiting period from him has ended and she then married another husband, then he has no way to her. But if she has not married, then she is his wife upon the first marriage.

key_terms.إِبَاقَ: the act of a slave fleeing or absconding from his master
key_terms.طَلَاقُ: divorce; here, the legal effect likened to the slave's escape
key_terms.عِدَّتُهَا: the waiting period observed by a woman after separation
key_terms.عِصْمَتُهَا: her marital bond and legal tie to her husband
key_terms.نَفَقَةٌ: financial maintenance due to a wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave flees from his master after marrying a free woman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slave who flees after marrying a free woman with his master's permission. It states that the wife is not entitled to maintenance from the master, and it explains the effect of the slave’s escape on the marital bond and the conditions under which the marriage may or may not resume if he returns.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4571 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hakam al-Ama and Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who permitted his slave to marry a free woman. The slave then fled from his master, and the wife of the slave came seeking maintenance from the master of the slave.
Imam (as) said: "She has no right to maintenance from the master of the slave, and her marriage bond with the slave is severed, because the slave's escape is considered a divorce, and he is like one who has apostatized from Islam."
I asked: "If the slave returns to his master, does his wife return to him?"
Imam (as) said: "If her waiting period (iddah) has ended and she has married another husband, then he has no claim over her. However, if she has not married another, she remains his wife based on the original marriage contract."
